_README: Human prose, one entry per game, merged into mechanics.json by scripts/arc3/mechanic_digest.py. This file is the ONLY part of the digest a machine does not derive, so re-running the extractor never overwrites it. Written by reading each game's source: `mechanic` is what the task is, `controls` is what each action does, `goal` is the win condition. SPOILERS by construction -- that is the point.

g007.mechanic: Bloxorz. A 1x2 block that stands upright or lies flat, rolled around a 16x16 floor with holes in it. Which cells it occupies depends on how it is lying, so the same move is safe standing and fatal lying down.
g007.controls: D-pad rolls the block. Nothing else is used.
g007.goal: Drop into the goal pit while UPRIGHT -- lying across it does not count. Broad plates need the block's weight spread flat; point plates need it standing. Rolling off the floor resets the level.

g030.mechanic: A ghost recorder. Your last five moves are kept on a tape; one press releases a ghost that replays them from where you started. The ghost is a second body that can stand on a pressure plate or trip a latch while you are somewhere else.
g030.controls: D-pad walks. ACTION5 releases the ghost, once per level -- the tape stops recording the moment you use it.
g030.goal: Reach the goal cell. Doors that need a plate held cannot be crossed alone, so the puzzle is choosing which five moves to leave on the tape.

g040.mechanic: A size gate. You carry a girth set by how many pips you have collected, and apertures in the walls only admit a body narrow enough to fit. Growing is what opens the exit and what closes the shortcuts.
g040.goal: Reach the exit once it is live. Pips are matched in coloured pairs, so which ones you take -- and in what order -- decides which apertures stay passable.

g026.mechanic: Timed moving voices create danger only where their loops overlap. Shared cells have persistent corner marks and become a bright crossed hazard while active. Collision and success frames settle visibly before transition. Original six levels plus a two-knot finale. Arrows move, ACTION5 waits.
g026.controls: D-pad moves; ACTION5 waits. Overlap markers become a bright crossed hazard when two voices coincide.
g026.goal: Reach the goal without standing on a sealed cell when it closes. Waiting is a real move and usually the point.

g036.mechanic: Lay an over/under cord along continuous tube paths. The second strand across a marked crossing must match its requested horizontal or vertical orientation. A six-move anchor lesson and a compact crossing lesson precede the original eight puzzles.
g036.controls: D-pad lays cord; junctions must be crossed straight. ACTION5 pulls tight at the green anchor. ACTION7 retracts using the visible finite pool. Ordinary path cells cannot be reused.
g036.goal: Reach the green anchor and pull with every marked crossing in the requested over/under order.

g035.mechanic: Layer clothing from inside out to pass colored hazards. Dark walls and five-pixel artwork sit over three-pixel movement cells. Two added chapters use shears and doors that require the exact remaining layer pattern, including holes and colors.
g035.controls: D-pad walks. ACTION5 wears the layer underfoot; on white shears it removes the outermost layer and returns it to its rack. The lower-left swatch shows the current remainder in pattern chapters.
g035.goal: Reach the white exit with an outfit that passes every colored or exact-pattern doorway.

g041.mechanic: A rotating maze. The board is a wheel whose mouths are linked in pairs; entering one puts you out at its partner and turns the whole frame by a recorded number of quarter-turns. Your controls rotate with it, so Up stops meaning up.
g041.controls: D-pad only. The direction you press is mapped through the current rotation.
g041.goal: Reach the goal. Tracking which way is which after two or three transits is the puzzle.

g022.mechanic: Triangular ember routing. Left/right move along those edges; up/down cross only the adjacent vertical edge, with the opposite direction inert. Five levels.
g022.controls: Left/right move along those edges. Up/down move only when that vertical edge is adjacent.
g022.goal: Reach the mould carrying EXACTLY the charge it asks for. Stepping onto it with the wrong charge does nothing at all -- no message, no death. Going past +/-3 in either direction resets the level, so the range is tight and the route is the arithmetic.

g011.mechanic: Native one-pixel slide animation with moving stones. The original seven tile maps remain; two later maps use a 64x64 collision grid with one- and two-pixel obstacles and off-grid resting goals.
g011.controls: D-pad starts a slide. Rest before the next move. Push stones one cell; pits swallow stones and switch crossings flip gate parity. ACTION7 is engine undo; the website's Z is its normal replay undo.
g011.goal: Come to rest on the cyan goal without falling into a pit.

g013.mechanic: Square movement and square growth propagation. Six compact ride puzzles require timed sowing, avoidable dead branches and up to three separately planted crossings. Six-pixel tiles and three visible cutting pips.
g013.controls: D-pad rides in a straight line. Click a socket to plant a cutting. Blocked moves wait one growth tick. The top pips show cuttings remaining.
g013.goal: Reach the goal. Cuttings are finite and blooms are temporary, so it is a timing puzzle: plant early and it has withered, plant late and you are standing still while it grows.

g016.mechanic: Ordered packet delivery with concurrent transit. Dispenser marks match receiver order; paired bottom marks identify faster lanes. Packet routes may bend and intersect. Shared advance_packets resolves speed, collisions and tied arrivals. Arrow movement/launch, ACTION5 waits. Nine levels.
g016.controls: D-pad walks or launches at a dispenser. ACTION5 waits. Every action advances all packets; double-marked dispensers launch faster packets.
g016.goal: Deliver every lane in order, then reach the exit. The board scrolls sideways, so part of the yard is off screen.

g015.mechanic: Triangular tool assembly. Left/right always move along those edges. Up/down act only when that vertical edge is adjacent. ACTION5 fires, ACTION6 takes a tool, ACTION7 waits. Seven levels.
g015.controls: Left/right follow the horizontal edges; up/down cross only an adjacent vertical edge. ACTION5 fires, ACTION6 takes a tool, ACTION7 waits.
g015.goal: Get a crate onto the goal cell. The puzzle is which pair to be holding when you reach the obstacle.

g014.mechanic: A block collapses into its directional shadow and raises every covered ground cell by one. White pips expose block height, blue inset edges expose depressions, and a pixel sweep shows the collapse. Six original puzzles.
g014.controls: Click a red block to collapse it. ACTION5 rotates the sun without collapsing; a collapse also rotates it. Other buttons do nothing.
g014.goal: Flatten every cell to height zero.

g047.mechanic: White exploration map with a visible red player and persistent revealed terrain. Four colored stations cast visible straight sight lines. Touch a station to select its mirror, then turn it clockwise with ACTION5. Green exits open only while reached by a live beam. Removed unrelated fittings and field noise.
g047.controls: D-pad moves the visible red player. Touch or stand beside a colored station to select its mirror; ACTION5 turns that mirror clockwise, even after walking away. Aim a live beam at the exit, then walk onto it.
g047.goal: Find the exit, illuminate it with one of the four mirrors, then walk onto it.

g009.mechanic: Triangular optical routing. A Y-shaped splitter emits two rays; mirrors emit one. Beam propagation animates cell by cell. Click a tray part to select it, click a socket to mount or remove it; ACTION5 cycles the tray. Six levels.
g009.controls: Click a tray part to select it, then click a socket to mount or remove it. ACTION5 cycles the tray.
g009.goal: Light every sink with the colour it asks for. The trace is recomputed and redrawn after every placement, so the beam is live feedback rather than a submission.

g037.mechanic: Cut and let fall. Blocks obey gravity and settle when what is under them goes; you face a direction and cut the cell in front, and everything above comes down. Heavy and light blocks fall differently.
g037.controls: Left and Right walk and face. Up and Down only change facing -- they do not move you. ACTION5 cuts the faced cell.
g037.goal: Clear every marker without losing one. A marker crushed or dropped out of reach is unrecoverable, so a cut in the wrong order ends the level quietly.

g043.mechanic: Square movement in all four directions. The blue ox pushes crates horizontally and the yellow mote swaps vertically with them. Portal cargo keeps sliding until blocked. Every exit is behind its plate-powered gate; both roles and the irreversible portal traps remain required.
g043.controls: D-pad moves the selected body. ACTION5 swaps bodies. The blue ox pushes horizontally; the yellow mote swaps vertically with a crate. Cargo entering a portal slides from its partner until blocked.
g043.goal: Reach the exit once the gates it needs are held open.

g032.mechanic: Mirrored sowing. Planting a seed plants a second one at the mirrored column, so every action you take happens twice, once on each side of an axis you are not shown. Plants age on a period and die.
g032.controls: D-pad walks. ACTION5 sows a seed where you stand. Walking onto a plant destroys it AND its mirror twin.
g032.goal: Reach the goal. Seeds are limited and the mirror means a plant you needed can be destroyed by walking somewhere unrelated on the other side.

g033.mechanic: A delivery round with a fixed sequence. Coloured crates go to bed stops down one side of the board, and the stops must be served in a REVERSE order set by the level -- the last one listed is the first one due.
g033.controls: D-pad walks and pushes. You carry one crate at a time.
g033.goal: Serve every stop in the required order. Serving the right crate at the wrong time is what loses the round, not dropping it.

g171.mechanic: Place or remove dams, then pour once to watch the full pixel BFS animation. Water is budgeted by complete cell rings. Three new mixing levels use blue and pink doses, removable plugs and exact tank targets; the last changes recipe after the first pour. Nine levels.
g171.controls: Click an open cell to place or remove a dam; click the source to pour. A normal pour runs to completion without further input. In mixing levels, click the marked valves to move plugs and match both tank targets; the last level changes recipe after its first pour.
g171.goal: Flood every basin within the tank budget. In mixing levels match the exact blue and pink quantities shown in the tanks, moving initial plugs as needed.

g017.mechanic: Restored seven square causeway puzzles. Collecting a white bead starts its ten-turn countdown; the tile then closes permanently. The ordering traps and progressively deeper networks are preserved.
g017.controls: D-pad moves on square causeways. ACTION5 waits; every lifted bead cell counts down for ten turns before closing.
g017.goal: Collect every white bead, then reach the mouth before a needed causeway hardens.

g034.mechanic: Layered stamps must reproduce the target exactly. Grid references, direct tray selection, full-size target comparison (ACTION4 or target click), and mismatch corners expose placement errors. ACTION5 cycles, ACTION6 places, ACTION7 undoes. Equality advances automatically; all eight levels have engine replays.
g034.controls: Click a tray stamp to select it; click the canvas to place it. ACTION5 cycles stamps, ACTION7 undoes. ACTION4 or clicking the target toggles a full-size comparison.
g034.goal: Match the target. Undo is built in, so this one is meant to be explored rather than solved first try.

g025.mechanic: Tools from pairs, again -- the larger sibling of g015. Six parts (magnet, rod, lens, torch, hook, bell) combine two at a time into abilities that burn vines, melt ice, grapple across gaps or ring a shutter open.
g025.controls: D-pad walks and faces. ACTION5 fires the held pair in the faced direction. ACTION6 drops what you hold, as a plain button with NO coordinates -- the other of the two tasks where clicking a cell is meaningless.
g025.goal: Reach the exit. Which two parts you are carrying decides which obstacle you can pass, and there is only one pair of hands.

g010.mechanic: Six original lantern maps and oil budgets with wider exploration: radius four at full light, three when dim, one at low fuel. Hidden terrain remains hidden until explored.
g010.controls: D-pad walks. Movement consumes oil; cyan cans refill it. Pink seals open the final gate.
g010.goal: Collect all three seals and reach the gate before oil runs out.

g028.mechanic: Fold geometry with key/lock overlays. A smaller first lesson teaches one fold. ACTION5 arms/commits, arrows walk or aim, click selects a crease, ACTION7 cancels. Preview marks the landing and camera magnifies the shrinking sheet. Levels 6-8 use visibly perforated midpoint seams: three folds, ordered V-V-H with prior movement, then four folds.
g028.controls: D-pad walks. ACTION5 arms a fold, arrows or a click choose the crease, and ACTION5 commits. ACTION7 cancels. Later sheets fold only on their marked midpoint seams.
g028.goal: Reach the exit by overlaying keys and locks. Level 7 requires two vertical folds before a horizontal fold, with a safe starting position; level 8 needs four folds.

g020.mechanic: Square-grid exploration with cyclic pulse/seal interactions. Six-pixel cells have a one-pixel row offset. The emitter strip pairs each pulse with the seal it dissolves; a wave shows where it travels. Only four arrow directions move; clicking a lamp emits. Six levels.
g020.controls: D-pad moves on four square-grid neighbours. Click an emitter to reveal routes and interact with seals. Its paired colour shows which seal it opens.
g020.goal: Reach the gate. Flares are the only information, so the game is about spending them where the map is ambiguous rather than where it is merely dark.

g006.mechanic: A chain reaction on a 32x32 field. Dots drift continuously on a wrapping field, each on its own heading. One detonation pops the nearest dot and chains outward to whatever is close enough to catch.
g006.controls: ACTION5 lets time pass -- the dots drift one step. CLICK A CELL to detonate at that point, and it only catches if a dot is within three cells -- one of the seven tasks where the click carries coordinates.
g006.goal: Set off a chain of at least the level's target size. You get one detonation, so this is a waiting game: let the drift bring the dots into a cluster, then click it.

g136.mechanic: Seven paired-tile puzzles at five pixels per tile, on a framed board. A spike is a red cross on both appearances of its tile, a warder target has amber warning corners, and sealing shows the lethal tile explicitly.
g136.controls: D-pad moves the selected keeper. ACTION5 selects the first keeper; ACTION7 selects the second. Each order also moves the warder. Amber corners indicate its current target; red crosses show danger on both paired appearances.
g136.goal: Hold every pressure plate down with crates AND stand on the exit at the same time. A pair that solves one plate usually breaks another, which is the whole difficulty.

g039.mechanic: A plugboard. Four sockets around the room carry cords between terminals, and pressing a socket advances its plug through a fixed cycle -- so one press rewires the room, not just that socket.
g039.controls: D-pad walks. ACTION5 presses the socket you are standing on.
g039.goal: Collect the keys, which lights the exit, and get there. Cords block or bridge depending on how they are patched, so the route is something you rewire rather than walk.

g044.mechanic: Seven-pixel square cells on a scrolling cube net. Matching colored cut edges connect when folded; crossing rotates the heading. Six orange keys open the green exit, blue arrows accept entry only in their direction. A net minimap and crossing particles make outer-edge travel visible. Level 3 requires folded travel.
g044.controls: D-pad moves on the current cube face. Crossing a colored cut edge wraps to its matching edge and rotates the heading. Blue arrows allow entry only in their direction. Collect all six orange keys, then enter the green exit.
g044.goal: Collect one orange key from each of the six cube faces and reach the green exit.

g027.mechanic: Triangular momentum transfer. Left/right retain screen direction. Up/down cross only the adjacent vertical edge. ACTION5 brakes and ACTION6 changes type. Six levels; adjacency and type interactions share helpers with the verifier.
g027.controls: Left/right shove in that direction. Up/down cross only the adjacent vertical edge. ACTION5 brakes; ACTION6 changes type.
g027.goal: Land every payload block in its socket. A payload in a pit ends the attempt -- speed is the thing to control.

g001.mechanic: A charge economy. Doors cost charges to open and the exit costs charges to use, out of one pool that does not refill. Every door you open is one you might not be able to afford to leave through.
g001.controls: D-pad walks and faces. ACTION5 spends charges on whatever you are facing -- a door, or the exit.
g001.goal: Leave through the exit with enough left to pay for it. The board shows each door's price, so this is a budgeting puzzle rather than a maze.

g024.mechanic: Control wrappers compose: double, turn, reverse and loop alter a directional action. Four new branching opening mazes need 14, 19, 22 and 41 actions; the later four pocket/reordering puzzles remain.
g024.controls: D-pad applies a direction through all worn wrappers. ACTION5 drops the outer wrapper on a green pocket; it can be picked up again to change order.
g024.goal: Reach the purple exit carrying at least the number of wrappers marked on it.

g023.mechanic: A click that means two things. Clicking YOUR OWN cell fires a plate; clicking any OTHER cell marks it. Same action, same button, entirely different effect depending on where it lands.
g023.controls: D-pad walks. ACTION5 fires a rod along the line you face. CLICK YOUR OWN SQUARE to fire a plate, CLICK ELSEWHERE to mark that cell -- one of the seven tasks where the click carries coordinates, and the only one where the target's identity changes what happens.
g023.goal: Open the exit and reach it. Discovering that the click is overloaded is most of the task.

g012.mechanic: Patrol timing and baited phase changes. The original six levels are preserved. Two wider scrolling levels add solid snake bodies that block movement and kill on contact. Arrow movement; ACTION5 waits. Eight levels.
g012.controls: D-pad moves. ACTION5 waits. All movement advances patrols; collecting a stone changes their route immediately.
g012.goal: Collect the coins to open the exit and get out. Waiting for a patrol to pass is usually better than outrunning it.

g045.mechanic: Timed portal pairs on a scrolling harbour of six-pixel cells. The top strip displays the three-phase connection schedule and separate four-phase D clock. Portal centers show active destinations; an ornate berth opens after cargo collection. Arrows enter mouths; ACTION5 waits in place without crossing. Seven levels.
g045.controls: D-pad moves and enters portals. ACTION5 waits without re-entering a portal. Every movement or wait advances the top schedule by one phase.
g045.goal: Collect every cargo crate, then enter the ornate berth. Its white center lights when all cargo is aboard.

g029.mechanic: Two bodies, one d-pad. You move both at once; the second one's direction is your direction reflected through a mirror axis, so pressing Left sends one body left and the other somewhere else. Neither moves unless BOTH have somewhere to go.
g029.controls: D-pad only. Pylons mark the axis and are spent as you pass them, which changes the reflection mid-level.
g029.goal: Get both bodies where they belong. A wall in front of one body freezes the pair, which is the lever you use to separate them.

g178.mechanic: Click the emitter to send a ball through self-switching junctions; click a junction to spend a manual flip. No avatar. Six-pixel balls and rails on black. Seven levels, ending with a branching tree and three-charge receivers.
g178.controls: Click the emitter to release a ball. Click a junction to spend one green manual-flip pip. The pulse itself flips each junction it passes. There is no walking control.
g178.goal: Charge every receiver. Its inset dots show the number of balls still needed; the final network has three-charge receivers.

g050.mechanic: Nine fog-and-ash puzzles with larger six-pixel cells, scrolling and clearer ember/masonry art. The first seven maps remain; two retrieval levels add single-use coolant orbs. Each orb buys one ash crossing, and every orb must be retrieved to open the exit.
g050.controls: D-pad moves. Leaving ordinary floor burns it; blue stone survives. In the last two levels collect every coolant orb, each of which lets you cross ash once.
g050.goal: Reach the exit without becoming trapped by ash. In coolant levels retrieve every orb first; collected doses each permit one crossing of burnt ground.

g019.mechanic: Square movement, square sound propagation and side-adjacent ballast transfer. Five refitted bell-and-plate puzzles retain conserved ballast, simultaneous plate targets and required re-ringing.
g019.controls: D-pad moves on the square board. Step on a bell to redirect the guards. ACTION6 waits one turn. Side-adjacent guards transfer ballast downhill; match all plate loads at once.
g019.goal: Stand on the exit with a guard parked on EVERY plate. You are not avoiding the patrol -- you are herding it onto the switches that open the way out.

g046.mechanic: Restored seven square patrol rooms. Filled pink patrols are current sightings; hollow dark-pink patrols are remembered positions outside sight. Walls block sight, and stale memories remain a genuine trap.
g046.controls: D-pad moves on square tiles. ACTION5 waits. Filled patrols are live sightings; hollow patrols are stale memories behind walls.
g046.goal: Reach the exit. The board is drawing you a stale picture on purpose; stale markers are drawn differently from live ones, and telling them apart is the task.

g042.mechanic: A barge on a chart. You steer a boat through a waterway of coloured locks, picking up cargo; a lock only lets you through once you are carrying what it is waiting for.
g042.goal: Lift all the cargo and pass the final lock. Locks are one-way in practice, so collecting in the wrong order strands you.

g031.mechanic: Stamping a key. You carry a shape that you can turn a quarter at a time, and mirrors on the board flip your handedness -- after passing one, Left moves you right and your shape is the mirror image. Sockets demand a specific handedness AND rotation.
g031.controls: D-pad walks (reversed while mirrored). ACTION5 turns your shape one quarter.
g031.goal: Fill every socket with the orientation it asks for, then leave. The mirrors are the only way to reach half the demands.

g005.mechanic: Points on a line, 16x16. A walker runs down a single path column and gates along it send it one way or the other; you set the gates before releasing it, and then it is out of your hands.
g005.controls: CLICK A GATE on the path column to flip it -- one of the seven tasks where the click carries coordinates, and only the path column responds. ACTION5 releases the walker.
g005.goal: Route the walker to the exit. Clicking anywhere off the path column does nothing at all, which reads as a broken click until you notice which cells respond.

g008.mechanic: Two-phase floor. You are red or blue, and cells of the other colour are solid to you. Swapping phase makes half the board appear and the other half vanish, and it cannot be done again for four turns.
g008.controls: D-pad walks. ACTION5 swaps your phase, subject to the cooldown.
g008.goal: Reach the exit. The cooldown is the puzzle -- swapping early strands you on the wrong colour for four moves.

g155.mechanic: Eight class-bite puzzles, preserving the original six. Persistent circular pixel fog reveals exploration. The two new terrain levels add one-way current arrows and magma that cools after eating cyan class 2; eating still removes every matching shelf.
g155.controls: D-pad moves; current arrows carry you downstream and cannot be walked against. ACTION5 eats the shelf underfoot. Eating cyan class 2 cools magma in the two new terrain levels.
g155.goal: Reach the exit. Biting is irreversible and the game resets the level as soon as it detects you can no longer get anywhere, so a wrong bite ends things immediately rather than later.

g162.mechanic: Six original sound-decoy puzzles are preserved. Each noisy step sends a visible wave through the room; sounders flash awake before the committed move resolves. Animation costs no extra action.
g162.controls: D-pad moves. Stepping on loose floor sends a sound wave and wakes the sounders. The wake-up animation is part of the same action.
g162.goal: Reach the exit. Loud tiles are often the direct route, so this is about choosing when to be heard and where you will be by the time they arrive.

g018.mechanic: Eight original woven-height/tide puzzles, followed by two embroidered-piece puzzles. Irregular cloth pieces rotate and fit sockets only when both geometry and cell weave match. The final three-gate route requires rotation and each installation.
g018.controls: D-pad walks. In the tide chapters, damp marks are cashed into a water rise when entering an arch. In the cloth chapters, click a nearby orange piece to carry it, ACTION5 rotates, and click its nearby matching cyan socket to install it. Click its original rack to return it.
g018.goal: Tide chapters: visit all arches and reach the summit. Cloth chapters: match every socket, open the linked gates, and reach the green exit.

g021.mechanic: Scale deduction with left/right pan placement and up/down crate selection. Click selects a crate; ACTION5 submits the LEFT pan to the connected target plate. Two material levels add light, heavy and volatile boxes; the latter shrink to mass one after three handling turns on a pan. Ten levels.
g021.controls: Left/right put the selected box on that pan, or return it home. Up/down select a box; clicking a box selects it too. ACTION5 submits the left pan. Handling turns consume a volatile box's three bright marks while loaded.
g021.goal: Submit the left-pan mass matching the connected target plate. Volatile boxes lose mass after three handling turns; the last two levels require using them before they fade.

g038.mechanic: A nonogram. An 8x8 board with a number beside every row and column; you fill cells until the counts work out. The purest click task in the set -- there is no character, no movement, nothing but the grid.
g038.controls: CLICK A CELL to fill or unfill it -- one of the seven tasks where the click carries coordinates, and the one with no alternative: it declares available_actions [5, 6, 7], so there is no d-pad at all. ACTION7 clears the board. ACTION5 checks your answer.
g038.goal: Satisfy every row and column clue. ACTION5 only advances you when the board is actually solved -- a wrong check costs nothing, so it is a check and not a commit.

g304.mechanic: A world up to 74x59 cells behind the 64x64 frame, which follows the avatar, so a screen position denotes a different world cell after the view has moved. The body is its own readout: its border is the avatar, its middle is the key it carries (colour for colour, pips for shape) and its corners are its gear. Floor plates restate the key, one family setting colour and another shape. Locks test both together and stay open. Purple plates light green when walked, and a gate opens once every rune colour in its quadrants is lit somewhere. Three pieces of gear lie about: boots make rubble walkable and rubble is wall without them, the blade kills the patrol you walk into and is spent doing it, the anchor keeps the key through a catch. Patrols come in two kinds -- orange hostiles send you home, teal wardens never touch you and kill any hostile they walk into. Bright pulsing plates that no rule reads are scattered through every level. Six levels.
g304.controls: ACTION1-4 walk the active avatar one cell. ACTION5 hands control to the other avatar on the levels that have two, from anywhere; walking into the idle body does the same, and on a one-body level ACTION5 is simply a wait that still steps every patrol. There is no click: the engine offers clickable targets in world coordinates with no camera offset subtracted, so on a scrolling world a human clicking the frame and an agent taking the offered coordinate would not be sending the same thing.
g304.goal: Enter the exit cell holding the key it shows, in both colour and shape. A hostile returns the active avatar to the last rune it lit with the key it started on; gear is never lost and open locks stay open, so a catch costs a long walk and never the run. The blade does not ask what it met, so spending one on a warden removes the thing that was clearing hostiles for you. From level four a second avatar keeps its own key, which is how a key reaches the exit after the first body has spent its own on a lock. Solver routes run 258 to 1001 moves.
